1.say: Read me your last sentence. 'Because the file had been moved, and the registrar had retired, nobody could confirm the date.' You made me wait for the point and it was worth waiting for. Do that once in a section. Only once? A page of them exhausts the reader. And never in a speech, where the listener cannot go back. Kamola says the same thing about long subjects. Kamola is right about most things. Now the list on page four. 'The role involves drafting reports, checking figures and to attend the committee.' Two of those are the same shape and the third is not. 'And attending the committee.' Good. Notice you fixed the odd one and left the other two alone. Half the people who see the fault rewrite the whole list instead. It would have taken longer and read worse. Most of my career could be described that way.

grammar.label: periodic and loose sentences — where the main clause goes
grammar.form: subordinate material first, main clause last (periodic); main clause first (loose)
grammar.meaning: controls whether the reader waits for the point or gets it at once

explanation.en: A periodic sentence holds the main clause until the end: 'Although the funds were approved in March, and the contractor appointed in April, the work did not begin.' A loose sentence delivers first and elaborates after. Periodic builds suspense and suits a conclusion; loose is easier to read and suits explanation. A page of either alone is exhausting.
explanation.uz: Davriy gap bosh gapni oxirigacha ushlab turadi; erkin gap avval aytadi, keyin izohlaydi. Davriy — kutish hosil qiladi, xulosaga mos; erkin — o'qish oson, tushuntirishga mos.

grammar.positive_example: Because the file had been moved, and the registrar had retired, nobody could confirm the date.
grammar.negative_example: Nobody could confirm the date because the file had been moved and because the registrar had retired and because nobody had kept a copy and because.

l1_notes.uz: Uzun ergash gaplarni oldinga qo'yish o'zbek tilida tabiiy (SOV tartibi), ingliz tilida esa o'quvchini charchatadi.

grammar.label: parallelism — diagnosing and repairing a broken list
grammar.form: matching grammatical form across coordinated or listed elements
grammar.meaning: keeps a list readable by making every item the same shape

explanation.en: B2 taught that coordinated items should match. C1 is the repair: find the odd item, decide which shape the list should take, and convert the others rather than the outlier. Comparisons break the same way — 'her method is better than Karimova' compares a method with a person, and the fix is 'than Karimova's'.
explanation.uz: B2 darajada teng qismlar mos kelishi kerakligi o'rgatilgan. C1 — tuzatish: mos kelmaydigan qismni topish va butun ro'yxatni bir shaklga keltirish.

grammar.positive_example: The role involves drafting reports, checking figures and attending the committee.
grammar.negative_example: The role involves drafting reports, checking figures and to attend the committee.

l1_notes.uz: Ro'yxatda shakl mosligi o'zbek tilida qo'shimchalar bilan avtomatik ta'minlanadi; ingliz tilida buni yozuvchi qiladi.

story.title: Because the file had been moved

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'Because the file had been moved, and the registrar had retired, nobody could confirm the date.'

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: You made me wait for the point and it was worth waiting for. Do that once in a section.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: A page of them exhausts the reader. And never in a speech, where the listener cannot go back.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Kamola says the same thing about long subjects.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Kamola is right about most things. Now the list on page four.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'The role involves drafting reports, checking figures and to attend the committee.'

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Two of those are the same shape and the third is not.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Good. Notice you fixed the odd one and left the other two alone. Half the people who see the fault rewrite the whole list instead.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It would have taken longer and read worse.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Most of my career could be described that way.
